podcast.title: Move to Los Angeles (2000)
podcast.body: Moved to Los Angeles in 2000 to work on the Tapeworm project with Trent Reznor. "Then in 2000, Atticus moved to LA to be part of a project with Trent called Tapeworm."

podcast.title: Songwriting Credit on "Old Town Road" (2019)
podcast.body: Atticus Ross received a songwriting credit for Lil Nas X's "Old Town Road" alongside Trent Reznor, Montero Hill (Lil Nas X), and Kioa Rokima (Young Kio). This credit stemmed from the song's use of a sample from Nine Inch Nails' instrumental "34 Ghosts 4," with Ross benefiting from the song's immense global success, including 18 million copies sold and billions of streams. "the songwriting credits for Old Town Road, you'll see that the writers are listed as Montero Hill, Kioa Rokima, the real name of Young Kio, plus Trent Risener and his songwriting partner Atticus Ross."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Songwriting Credit on "Old Town Road" (2019)
podcast.body: As Trent Reznor's songwriting partner, Atticus Ross was given songwriting credits for Lil Nas X's "Old Town Road" following a quiet negotiation, sharing in the song's profits and Grammy wins. "Trent and his songwriting partner, Atticus Ross, were given songwriting credits on Old Town Road and thus a share of the profits."

podcast.title: Academy Awards, Golden Globes, Emmy
podcast.body: Atticus Ross has won two Academy Awards, three Golden Globes, and an Emmy for his film and TV scoring work, primarily with Trent Reznor. "A Golden Globe and an Academy Award for Best Original Score."

podcast.title: Co-holder of Billboard Hot 100 Record
podcast.body: As co-composer of "34 Ghosts 4," the source material for Lil Nas X's "Old Town Road," Atticus Ross (with Trent Reznor) shares the record for the pop song with the most weeks (19) at number one on the Billboard Hot 100. "As a result, both Trent and Atticus Ross, co-composers of the original source material, 34 goes for, were given official songwriting credits on Old Town Road, and therefore sharing all the chart records of the song."

podcast.body: The experience with Tapeworm, despite not resulting in a release, must have been positive, as Atticus Ross has worked on every Nine Inch Nails album since "With Teeth" (2005). "Atticus has worked on every 9-H nails album since with Teeth in 2005."

xref.title: Supergroup Lineup and Origins (1994-2001)
xref.body: Tapeworm was conceived as a side project during Nine Inch Nails' "The Downward Spiral" sessions in 1994, intended as a collaborative effort for Danny Lohner and Charlie Clouser. It evolved to include a star-studded lineup: Trent Reznor, Maynard James Keenan (Tool), producer Alan Molder, Atticus Ross, Phil Anselmo and Rex Brown (Pantera), Page Hamilton (Helmet), Toni Halliday (Curve), Tommy Victor (Ministry), and drummer Josh Freese, with at least an album's worth of material recorded by 2001. "If you're Trent Rezner, Danny Loaner and Charlie Closer from his live band, Maynard James Keenan from Tool, producer Alan Molder and Atticus Ross. I mean, wow, awesome, right? The idea for tapeworm went as far back as the sessions for the downward spiral in 1994. Tapeworm was designed as something to which Danny and Charlie could contribute as equals. This idea evolved into something pretty cool. Maynard was brought in, Phil and Salmo from Pantera, Paige Hamilton from Helmut, Tony Haliday from a cool band called Curve, Tommy Victor from Ministry, drummer Josh Freeze. And then in 2001, Alan Molder apparently helped record at least an album's worth of stuff."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Project History (1995-2004)
xref.body: This project was created in 1995 and involved Trent Reznor, Atticus Ross, and a variety of friends, continuing off and on for nine years. Despite the collaboration, nothing was ever officially released. "I already mentioned the tapeworm project, which was created in 1995 and included a lot of different friends. They were continued off and on for nine years, but nothing was ever released."

xref.title: Songwriting Credit on "Old Town Road" (2019)
xref.body: Trent Reznor holds the record for the most weeks at the top of the Billboard Hot 100 singles chart due to his songwriting credit on Lil Nas X's "Old Town Road." His involvement stemmed from the song's beat sampling the instrumental track "34 Ghosts 4" from Nine Inch Nails' 2008 album "Ghosts I–IV," with Reznor granting permission for the sample and receiving credit alongside his songwriting partner Atticus Ross. "Trent listened to Old Town Road and declared it to be unbelievably catchy, so he said, yeah, go ahead and use it, but I need a songwriting credit, which is very reasonable."

xref.title: Financial Success from "Old Town Road"
xref.body: As a credited songwriter for "Old Town Road," Trent Reznor, along with Atticus Ross, has benefited significantly from the song's massive global success, which includes 18 million copies sold worldwide, millions of radio plays, 1.5 billion YouTube views, and over 3 billion streams. He is simply "cashing the jacks" from the royalties generated by the track. "And Trent and Risener, he's just sitting at home, caching the jacks."
